what_happened: Precisely isolated and reproduced prune_next_body()'s flag-misparse defect via a standalone awk harness replaying the real function: gsub(/[ \t]/, "", tasklist) fuses a trailing CLI flag onto the last task id (e.g. '714 --hard' -> '714--hard'), which never matches the active-ids lookup. Confirmed four failure shapes incl. the worst case -- total silent disappearance of a single-task flagged Run line (kept=0, n2=1, neither output branch fires). Also found and confirmed an identical sibling defect in count_pruned_next_ids() (jq -e --argjson errors on the fused non-numeric token, exit 2, misread as 'not active'), corrupting the pruned=/retained= stderr diagnostic counters via the same root cause. Confirmed zero existing test coverage of flag-bearing Run lines in either layout's --prune test group.

Research Recommendation 1 proposed splitting the Run line's pre-rationale portion on the first run of whitespace; that would mis-split the grammar-legal '/orchestrate 716, 714 --hard' (the documented Next Grammar admits intra-list spaces via [\d, ]+) into tasklist='716,' and flags='714 --hard', introducing a second content-loss path. The plan narrows the approach to anchor segmentation on the first whitespace-preceded '-' instead, and adds an intra-list-space fixture.

The research report's byte-for-byte reproduction harness and five-input Expected/Actual table let the planning phase skip a dedicated red-baseline phase entirely and write exact-output verification criteria directly, with only a Scope Hypothesis to re-confirm the carried byte-identical-deploy-mirror claim.

covered_ids_from() (roadmap-integration.sh, ~line 523) scrapes all digits from the whole Run line including rationale prose and numeric flag arguments (e.g. --max-tasks 8), mis-attributing them as covered task ids; out of scope for task 388, which only fixes prune_next_body()/count_pruned_next_ids()
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'specs/388_prune_next_body_flag_misparse_drops_active_task/issues.jsonl' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.
